authorization: User requested all 122 whole practice questions from Linear Relationships; teaching content excluded.
method: Ordinary promotion in isolated staging, verified once and published through a checked transaction.

classification.difficultyReason: Compare explicitly labelled coordinate pairs and identify the constant y-coordinate on the horizontal line and constant x-coordinate on the vertical line.

questions.mappingNote: plot-points-cartesian is the closest supplied skill because students identify coordinate properties of displayed points. No supplied skill specifically names coordinate invariance on horizontal and vertical lines. Graph construction and equation generation are not assessed.

classification.difficultyReason: Connects two completed tables and coincident graphs to explain why different input choices produce the same line. Finding further points and justifying x=100 require applying the equation beyond the displayed grid, with the preceding parts supplying substantial scaffolding.

questions.mappingNote: graph-linear-relationship is primary because students construct and compare the resulting lines. construct-table-of-values, linear-representations, plot-points-cartesian and point-satisfies-line are directly assessed by completing tables, explaining the common equation and graph, plotting coordinates, and producing or verifying further points. Comparing slopes or intercepts of different equations is not required.

questions.note: In (a), the diagram code plots (-2,3), (0,3), (2,3) and (4,3) on y=3: every second coordinate is 3. In (b), it plots (2,-2), (2,0), (2,2) and (2,4) on x=2: every first coordinate is 2. Both supplied answers and explanations are correct. Explicit coordinate labels make the task self-contained; identifying the invariant coordinate follows the supplied axis and plotting teaching.

Substituting into y=2x+1 gives (a) y=-3,1,5 for x=-2,0,2 and (b) y=-1,3,6 for x=-1,1,2.5. In (c), all six pairs lie within the supplied axes and satisfy the same linear equation, so their extended straight lines coincide. The solution code correctly plots all six points and y=2x+1, meeting the frame at (-2.5,-4) and (3.5,8). In (d), the supplied further points (0.5,2) and (3,7) are distinct from the earlier points and satisfy the equation. In (e), x=100 gives y=201, so (100,201) belongs to the extended line despite lying outside the displayed grid. All supplied answers are correct. The task supplies its equation, tables and axes; its methods match the teaching on substitution, coordinate pairs, plotting and extending straight lines.
